# 1 Clement Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 5

**[TRANSLATOR'S NOTE: This chapter contains the earliest non-NT reference to the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul, written c. 96 CE — within living memory of the events. These verses are among the most historically significant in all early Christian literature.]**

**5:1** But to cease from ancient examples, let us come to the champions of the most recent times. Let us take the noble examples of our own generation.

**5:2** Because of jealousy and envy the greatest and most righteous pillars were persecuted and contended unto death.

**5:3** Let us set before our eyes the good apostles:

**5:4** Peter, who because of unrighteous jealousy endured not one or two but many labors, and thus having given his testimony went to the glorious place which was his due.

**5:5** Because of jealousy and strife Paul showed the way to the prize of patient endurance:

**5:6** Seven times he bore chains; he was exiled; he was stoned; he was a herald in both the East and the West; he won noble renown for his faith;

**5:7** Having taught righteousness to the whole world and having come to the extreme limit of the West, and having borne testimony before the rulers, he was thus set free from the world and went to the holy place, having become the greatest example of patient endurance.

---

*EMET: "the extreme limit of the West" almost certainly refers to Spain, indicating Paul reached his intended destination (Rom 15:24, 28). "Gave his testimony" and "bore testimony" — both use the Greek root for martyrdom, *martyrion*. "Glorious place" = Paradise/Heaven. Seven chains, exile, stoning — details not in the canonical Acts.*
